title: The Case of the Diary Left Open
slogan: AI NEWS · HUMAN-CENTRED · HUMANS IN CONTROL
music: Slow black-and-white film-noir jazz: lonely muted trumpet, soft upright bass, brushed drums, rain mood, minor key, no vocals.
ambience: Night rain on an empty city street, distant traffic hiss, a buzzing neon sign, no music.

shots.say: Case three. A confession, typed alone at night. Where do our secrets go when we tell them to a machine?

sfx.prompt: A car driving slowly past on a wet street at night, tires on water
Slow footsteps on wet pavement at night

shots.say: June twenty twenty-five. People pour their lives into Meta's AI app. Health worries. Legal trouble. Then they tap a button called share.

sfx.prompt: Soft phone screen keyboard typing taps in a quiet room
Single soft phone screen tap with a subtle confirmation click

shots.say: Those chats could land on a public feed called Discover. Some showed addresses and phone numbers. Meta says chats are private by default, and you have to choose to share.

sfx.prompt: Murmuring crowd under umbrellas in the rain in a city square

shots.say: Critics said the button never made clear where the words would go. Meta added a warning: prompts you post are public.

ov.text: “Prompts you post are public and visible to everyone.”

sfx.prompt: Flickering neon sign buzzing and clicking in a rainy alley

shots.say: So before you confess to a machine: read the button. Check the settings. And remember, a chatbot is not a diary with a lock.

items: Read the button before you tap
Check who can see your chats
A chatbot is not a locked diary

sfx.prompt: Old wall clock ticking slowly in a quiet dark room

shots.say: Privacy isn't a setting you find once. It's a habit. Case closed.

sfx.prompt: Single heavy rubber stamp thud on paper on a wooden desk
